question: GCF-18/20 looked wrongly split and GCF-27 wrongly merged. How widespread is either failure across the run?
dataset: Enterobacterales RefSeq, 1,303 BGCs, 72 families, 10 kb neighbourhood
answer: Rare. Of 44 families with >=4 members, 41 are sound and 3 are flagged -- 2 chimeric, 1 wrongly split. The clustering is mostly right, and the two cases that prompted this are close to the whole of the problem.

two_diagnostics_are_needed_because_one_i.gene_content_cohesion: mean pairwise Jaccard over orthologue-group content between a family's members. Low = the members do not share genes = the family is several clusters.
two_diagnostics_are_needed_because_one_i.internal_vs_external_distance: median BiG-SCAPE distance within the family against the median to the nearest other family in the same connected component. Internal > external = the family is further from itself than from its neighbour.
two_diagnostics_are_needed_because_one_i.why_both: Internal > external ALONE does not identify over-splitting: a chimeric family fails it too, because merging unlike things inflates internal diversity. Crossed with cohesion the two modes separate -- LOW cohesion with high internal diversity means wrongly merged; HIGH cohesion with high internal diversity means wrongly split.

flagged.verdict: WRONGLY MERGED, and an extreme outlier -- the next worst cohesion in the run is 0.42. Splits into 21 sub-clusters at Jaccard 0.45, 16 of them singletons, the largest holding 13 of 38. Within-subcluster Jaccard 0.44 against 0.05 between, a ninefold gap. The alignment shows three architectures: two PF01066 upstream at -12/-9 kb (the confirmed phosphonolipid, LMG 5342 and VY148), one PF01066 downstream at +11 kb with a distinct accessory block, and a third with no PF01066 and a different block entirely. 505 orthologue groups across 38 members is the fingerprint.

Chimeric by cohesion but it PASSES the distance test (internal 0.321 < external 0.559), so it is not being confused with a neighbour. 6 sub-clusters, largest 46%. The 10-gene redox module at prevalence 0.46 reported earlier is this sub-structure. Weaker case than GCF-27.

WRONGLY SPLIT, the clearest case. Confirmed independently: cross-family pepM identity 0.975 against GCF-18's own internal 0.974, and 19 of 23 proteins homologous at 93-100%. See ../pantaphos_three_families/sequence_evidence.json.

what_this_retracts: An earlier reading of GCF-27 attributed its low PF01066 prevalence (0.16) to contig truncation -- 71% of members lacking the gene are contig-edge against 21% of those carrying it. The correlation is real but confounded: the truncated members are mostly the third architecture, which lacks PF01066 for architectural reasons. Full-length non-truncated members lack it too (Dickeya dadantii LMG 27546 at 34 CDS, D. dadantii XJ12 at 33, Yersinia wautersii WP-931201 at 38). Prevalence is low because the family is three clusters, not because its members are fragments.

consequences.prevalence_in_a_chimeric_family_is_meani: 0.16 for PF01066 in GCF-27 averages three architectures. Within the one that has it, it is effectively 1.0.
consequences.the_consensus_for_GCF_27_describes_no_re: Its gene list and diagram are an average of unlike things.
consequences.a_proposed_fix_was_aimed_at_the_wrong_th: Computing prevalence over intact members only would have corrected a denominator that was not the problem.

method_note: Families with <4 members are not assessed; pairwise cohesion over 3 points is not informative. Distances come from the run's own BiG-SCAPE database. Cohesion comes from gcf_annotation_transfer.tsv's orthologue groups, which is why the per-CDS group id was added to that file.

data.gcf27_alignment.svg: all 38 GCF-27 members aligned on pepM and flipped so it reads left to right; black = PF01066, red = contig edge
data.gcf27_align.py: the script that drew it; a recorded experiment, not a pipeline stage

GCF_5_retired_2026_10_05: GCF-5 was flagged as marginally over-split against GCF-6, on an internal-vs-external margin of 0.009. Removed: five replicate runs of its connected component put that well inside run-to-run jitter. See ../bigscape_reproducibility/summary.json.
